subject: Post-call: regional routing & performance gating for FinSecure
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.it>, Marta Alvarez <m.alvarez@finsecure.it>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: regional routing, perf targets, next steps

Hi Elena / Marta —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the asks we promised: we covered your high-level SLO targets and routing constraints and sketched what a proof-of-concept (POC) would look like. Below are the concrete items we captured on the call and a couple of clarifying questions.

Summary of your stated targets (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for non-streaming short completions (<=128 tokens) in US and EU; p95 <= 400ms target in APAC.
- Streaming: initial token latency (first-byte) p95 <= 200ms in US/EU, sustained token throughput 30–50 tokens/sec per stream.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 200 rps across US/EU with ability to burst to 800 rps; sustained concurrent streaming sessions ~150 per region with 30 minute spikes to 500.
- Data residency: EU customer payloads and logs must be retained in EU (customer-managed keys preferred); APAC data must not leave APAC unless explicitly redacted.
- Failover/routing: primary region routing by source IP -> geo routing; fallback to another region only with explicit approval or during capacity emergency (and must be logged).

Clarifying questions we need from you to size the POC:
1) Your expected average prompt length and average completion length (tokens) for the mid-tier workflows? (helps with token/sec and batching profiles)
2) Any hard SLA penalties around p95? (useful for recommending Dedicated vs Hosted)
3) Will you require fixed IP allowlists for your outbound callbacks or webhooks?

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO spreadsheet (SLO-table-FinSecure.xlsx) with columns for per-region targets, expected traffic profile, and an initial cost/throughput sizing. Also included a short sample network trace we discussed.

Next steps (proposed):
- FinSecure: confirm answers to the 3 clarifying questions above (Elena) — due Wed 12/02 EOD.
- Redwood: provide a POC proposal with target capacity, latency gating plan, and a mutual action plan (MAP) — we’ll aim to send the first draft by Thurs 12/03.
- Security: Laura will follow up with SOC2/ISO evidence and a short note on key management options.

If those items look right I’ll kick off a brief MAP doc and scope a 2-week POC that runs a targeted workload against Dedicated capacity in EU + burst from US/APAC for failover testing.

Thanks — talk soon,

Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SLO-table-FinSecure.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-trace-example.txt (text)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.it>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Alvarez <m.alvarez@finsecure.it>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: regional routing, perf targets, next steps

Thanks Alex — useful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Token/profile: mid-tier workflows average ~40 tokens in prompt and ~120 tokens returned on average. Peak long-form flows (report generation) can be ~800 tokens but are <5% of traffic.
- SLA: we do not plan to include financial penalties in the POC, but we need a clear escalation timeline (TTR targets) and uptime guardrails before moving to production.
- Routing & data flow: EU traffic must stay in EU for both request/response payloads and logs. For analytics aggregations that are strictly anonymized and never include raw payloads, we may allow transfer to US for storage, but only after approval from our legal/compliance team.

Questions:
1) For APAC: you mentioned Singapore vs Tokyo regions — do you recommend both, or is one preferred for a low-latency path to our Hong Kong and Melbourne users?
2) For streaming: can we enforce a per-request token rate limit on the server side so that a single long-running stream cannot consume more than X tokens/sec? We want predictable capacity during major spikes.

We’re fine with the MAP approach. I’ll confirm internal contacts for legal/compliance and share them by tomorrow.

—Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Engineering, FinSecure
elena.rossi@finsecure.it

From: priyom_das@redwood.com <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.it>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: regional routing, perf targets, next steps

Hi Elena — good questions. Short answers and what we can commit for the POC: 

APAC region recommendation:
- Singapore (asia-southeast1) gives the best balance for SE Asia and Australia (Melbourne). Tokyo (asia-northeast1) is slightly better for Japan/Hokkaido. For a single-region POC we typically recommend Singapore to capture HK/Melbourne with lower median latency; if Japan is critical we can run a dual-region edge with smart routing.

Streaming rate limiting / per-request throttles:
- Yes — we can enforce server-side rate limits and token throttles per stream. Typical enforcement options: token-rate cap per stream (tokens/sec), total concurrent token budget per customer, and soft-queueing with guaranteed minimal throughput. For the POC we can set a conservative token cap of 50 tokens/sec per stream and a global streaming concurrency quota (150) with burst capacity gates.

Data residency / logging:
- For the POC we can keep request/response payloads and non-PII logs in-region (EU, APAC). For anonymized metrics (aggregates, histograms) we can allow transfer to Redwood-hosted analytics in the US on an opt-in basis; we’ll include that as a toggle in the MAP. Key management: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for the Dedicated deployment.

Work items we’ll take on:
- Technical sizing doc (incl. expected instance types, batching knobs, and expected p95 numbers under your token profile).
- POC config: Dedicated pool in EU, test nodes in SG for APAC traffic, routing rules, and a monitoring dashboard with token-level cost/latency breakdown.

I’ll attach an initial perf runbook to the MAP draft.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Marta Alvarez <m.alvarez@finsecure.it>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.it>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: regional routing, perf targets, next steps

Thanks Priyom — that helps. A couple of procurement items so we can move the POC along: 

- Can you confirm whether the POC will require a purchase order or if we can operate under a time-limited evaluation agreement? Our procurement prefers a PO for any dedicated capacity but legal can accept a limited evaluation contract if Redwood agrees to scoped telemetry and security clauses.
- Please include an estimated cost range for the 2-week POC in the MAP draft so procurement can provision a PO quickly.

Also, Laura — could you send the SOC2 snapshot and the list of redaction/censoring capabilities for logs? We need that for our compliance submission.

Thanks,
Marta

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <m.alvarez@finsecure.it>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finsecure.it>
Cc: alex.martinez@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T20:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: regional routing, perf targets, next steps

Hi Marta / Elena —

I’ve uploaded a SOC2 Type II evidence packet and a short security FAQ to the shared link: https://redwood-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/documents/SLO-table-FinSecure.xlsx (see tab "Security & Evidence"). Key points: 
- SOC2: we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report under NDA; I’ll send the NDA template if you want to proceed.
- Log redaction: our ingestion pipeline supports configurable redaction rules (regex + PII detectors) at edge; you can choose to drop request/response payloads from logs, store only hashed request IDs, or keep full payloads in-region under CMK.
- DOCS: We also have a one-pager on KMS integrations and an example KMS key rotation schedule.

Regarding procurement: we can support either a short evaluation agreement or a PO for Dedicated POC. I’ll include both options in the MAP draft with an estimated range for a 2-week Dedicated EU + SG test (ballpark: $18k–$28k depending on instance types and burst bandwidth). Exact numbers will be in the MAP.

Next steps for us:
- Redwood to share MAP draft + sizing (target: 12/03).
- FinSecure to confirm token profile and legal/compliance contacts (Elena to share by 12/02).
- Schedule a 30-min followup tech call to finalize region selection (we propose Thurs 12/03 10:00 PT / Fri 12/04 18:00 CET).

Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Forwarded-attachments: SLO-table-FinSecure.xlsx, network-trace-example.txt
